articles.title_orig: The open-source AI platforms vying to become China’s Hugging Face
articles.title_zh: The open-source AI platforms vying to become China’s Hugging Face
articles.content_orig:
For Beijing, managing AI requires walking a razor’s edge: seal off domestic internet users from foreign influence, but keep China’s top developers linked to the global cutting edge.
When Chinese regulators blocked U.S.-based open-source hub Hugging Face in 2023, it opened a market for domestic alternatives —  even as the government quietly tolerates artificial intelligence labs bypassing the block to share Chinese models with the world.
In the AI era, China is developing an independent ecosystem faster than in the internet era.” Xu Yong, chief executive of OSChina
Alibaba i Alibaba Alibaba, founded in 1999 by Chinese entrepreneur Jack Ma, is one of the most prominent global e-commerce companies that operates platforms like AliExpress, Taobao, and Tmall. READ MORE had launched a Hugging Face-like open-model platform, ModelScope, in 2022, which now hosts more than 170,000 models. Tech company OSChina launched another open-model site, MoArk, in 2023, serving some 20,000 models.
“Not everyone is able to use a VPN [virtual private network] all the time,” Xu Yong, chief executive of OSChina, told Rest of World . Just as China’s internet industry had flourished behind the Great Firewall, the country also needed to build a self-reliant AI ecosystem to serve the Chinese-speaking population, Xu said.
“In the AI era, China is developing an independent ecosystem faster than in the internet era,” Xu said.
Unlike closed models from OpenAI and Anthropic, which are only accessible through their companies, open models can be downloaded, fine-tuned, and deployed on local hardware.
There is still this real concern in China that access to [the U.S.-based platforms] could be disrupted at any point.” Rebecca Arcesati, researcher with the think tank Mercator Institute for China Studies
New York-based Hugging Face has become the most popular place to share open models and data sets. In September, Nvidia announced it was acquiring Hugging Face for $12.9 billion, as the chipmaker bets on growing adoption of open-source models.
Beijing regulators did not disclose a specific reason when it blocked access to Hugging Face, but the Chinese government routinely blocks foreign websites that can host information it deems harmful. Chinese authorities occasionally penalized citizens for circumventing the Great Firewall without authorization. But VPN use is common in the tech industry, as developers need to access blocked sites such as Google and X in their work.
Chinese programmers have turned to global open-source platforms to share texts and images that would be censored at home. On GitHub, the Microsoft-owned platform that hosts open-source code, Chinese programmers have staged protests against long working hours and preserved news articles about Covid-19 lockdowns that had been removed from the Chinese internet.
China briefly blocked GitHub in 2013, triggering an outcry from programmers. Access was later restored. The government in 2020 endorsed Gitee, a domestic version of GitHub also owned by OSChina. But GitHub remains popular in China as the gateway to the global software community.
Rebecca Arcesati, a Brussels-based researcher with the think tank Mercator Institute for China Studies, said the Chinese government recognized that access to international open-source platforms was important to the development of its tech industry.
Chinese AI companies have been releasing powerful open models on Hugging Face so they can be downloaded and deployed across the world. Developers in China also need to access open models shared by people outside China.
At the same time, the government also believes that domestic platforms are more secure and reliable than those controlled by American companies and subject to U.S. regulations.
The Trump administration, which is keen on ensuring America’s lead in AI, has reportedly discussed bans on Chinese models. In a regulatory filing about the acquisition of Hugging Face, Nvidia flagged the risk that regulators could ban Chinese models from being shared on the site.
“There is still this real concern in China that access to [the U.S.-based platforms] could be disrupted at any point,” Arcesati said. “From the Chinese government’s perspective, it will be ideal if the entire technology stack for AI, including the software tools and libraries, could be indigenized as much as possible.”
Both ModelScope and MoArk offer services similar to Hugging Face, including model testing and customization. They offer some free usage and charge users for extra computing power and advanced features.
But the number of models on the two Chinese platforms still fall far behind Hugging Face, which hosts more than 3 million open models. ModelScope said in March that it had 170,000 models and 250 million users. Xu said MoArk hosted more than 20,000 commonly used models.
To attract users, ModelScope has hosted university hackathons, where students compete to build AI applications. It also opened a coworking and event space in Hangzhou for AI entrepreneurs.
The Chinese AI industry has faced a shortage of computing power as the U.S. has banned sales of top AI chips to China. Several local companies are now racing to build advanced chips.
MoArk has deployed a team of engineers to adapt AI models to run on different types of Chinese chips, as a way to establish itself as part of China’s own AI ecosystem, according to Xu. “It’s our mission to make sure mainstream open models can run on Chinese chips,” Xu said.
AI developers in China say the main attraction of the domestic platforms is faster download speeds, though they still prefer accessing Hugging Face with a VPN. “Hugging Face and GitHub are the default in the open-source space. They offer a greater variety,” Chen Yunfei, an independent AI developer in Kunming, told Rest of World. “Domestic platforms need to convince us why we should use them.”
The Emirates owns the machines but rents the intelligence. Nvidia’s next free AI model could change that.
In an excerpt from his book, “Innovate for Impact: A Roadmap to Sustainable Technology Beyond AI,” Alessandro Crimi explains that a tax on automation is more effective than retraining labor.
Samsung and SK Hynix dominate the high-bandwidth memory market. Now they are competing to become indispensable to Nvidia, OpenAI, and other U.S. AI companies.

articles.title_orig: Smart ring maker Oura postpones IPO due to market 'uncertainty'
articles.title_zh: Smart ring maker Oura postpones IPO due to market 'uncertainty'
articles.content_orig:
Oura has said that it is delaying plans for its public listing on the Nasdaq due to uncertainty in the IPO market.
The delay comes despite "strong demand" and a strengthening of the business since the start of the IPO process, the company said in a statement on Tuesday.
The company, which makes a smart ring that tracks wearers' health and sleep, formally launched its IPO plans just last week on Sept. 21.
At the time, the company planned to raise up to $2.2 billion with the sale of 50 million shares.
"Our mission is to empower people to live healthier, longer, and an IPO is just one step in our journey," said CEO Tom Hale on Tuesday.
"We aim to deliver an extraordinary IPO for our employees and investors and we have the luxury of choosing our moment ," he added . "In the meantime, we will execute against the opportunities ahead."
Oura is profitable, the company said, with revenue expected to grow 90% year over year for the fiscal year 2026.
Launched in 2015, Oura's smart ring has evolved well beyond sleep tracking and now features a variety of features focused on broader health and wellness. In recent years, it has increasingly focused on advancing preventative health through new capabilities, AI, analytics and other features.
Oura is the latest U.S. public market hopeful to delay an IPO in recent weeks. Holtec Nuclear withdrew its IPO earlier this month citing adverse market sentiment in equity markets.
Holtec said that uncertainty over data development compounded "pre-existing headwinds, including rising energy costs, elevated global trade tensions, ongoing military conflicts, and mounting inflation fears that have driven the central banks of major economies (EU, Japan and US) to raise their benchmark rates."
Oura's IPO postponement outlines the "challenges facing issuers in an increasingly turbulent market," Samuel Kerr, global head of ECM at Mergermarket, told CNBC. "Rising sovereign debt yields are spooking investors and causing some to ask for far wider discounts to offset any pressure on future earnings from rising WACC [weighted average cost of capital]."

articles.title_orig: Could Trump revoke Ilhan Omar's citizenship for alleged brother marriage? Ex federal prosecutor breaks it down
articles.title_zh: Could Trump revoke Ilhan Omar's citizenship for alleged brother marriage? Ex federal prosecutor breaks it down
articles.content_orig:
Immigration attorney Michael Wildes explains the evidence required to establish marriage fraud and whether Omar’s claim that DHS has not contacted her impacts the legitimacy of the investigation.
The Trump administration's recent effort to bring the law down on Rep. Ilhan Omar could go as far as seeking to strip the Minnesota congresswoman of her citizenship for alleged immigration fraud. But a criminal investigation is unlikely to yield the results the president wants, according to a former federal prosecutor.
Michael Wildes, an immigration attorney, told Fox News Digital that investigators face a "very high bar" to build a case against Omar after White House border czar Tom Homan confirmed the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) is conducting a "criminal" investigation against the progressive "Squad" member.
It all stems from claims that Omar married her brother to gain U.S. citizenship, which she has repeatedly denied.
President Donald Trump has a longstanding feud with Omar going back to when she was first elected in the middle of his first term, and quickly became one of his most vocal critics in Congress. Trump has repeatedly called for Omar to be sent back to Somalia because of her alleged fraudulent activity.
The Trump administration continues to ramp up efforts to denaturalize and deport individuals accused of immigration fraud. And Vice President JD Vance claimed earlier this year that the Department of Justice is investigating Omar for alleged fraud and immigration violations.
But questions remain over what a potential prosecution and denaturalization case against the Somali-born lawmaker would require.
Wildes said that investigators would need to prove beyond reasonable doubt that Omar knowingly entered her marriage — to a man critics allege is her brother — for the sole purpose of evading U.S. immigration laws.
DOJ MOVES TO STRIP CITIZENSHIP FROM 17 PEOPLE ACCUSED OF HIDING DISTURBING CRIMES
U.S. Representative Ilhan Omar speaks during Day 2 of the Minnesota Democratic-Farmer-Labor (DFL) Party Convention in the Mayo Civic Center in Rochester, Minn., on Saturday, May 30, 2026. (Alex Kormann/The Minnesota Star Tribune via Getty Images)
"In order to establish a successful marriage fraud case, the government would have to prove beyond a reasonable doubt… that the defendant knowingly entered into a marriage with the primary purpose to evade immigration laws and get a benefit," Wildes said.
Wildes noted that even if Omar and her husband, Ahmed Nur Said Elmi, decided after getting married that their partnership could be a scheme for Elmi to fast pass America’s immigration process, this would not be considered marriage fraud in court.
He continued, "Those are very high bars and thresholds that they would have to surmount. The immigration benefit cannot be a byproduct or secondary consideration. This is not deemed to be illegal."
If evidence was presented to prove Omar and Elmi committed marriage fraud , the Minnesota Democrat could face up to five years in jail, a maximum fine of $250,000, or both.
Wildes also pointed out that there are statutes of limitations that could hinder a potential prosecution and make it more difficult to prosecute Omar for marriage fraud, as that marriage was in 2009. But there is still a pathway for Omar to be denaturalized, which Homan described as a "very serious process" while discussing the investigation into the congresswoman.
"The question is: Do they have it factually, and is it the right thing to do?" Wildes said.
"The question is whether or not inadvertences were made not purposefully and whether or not it's over the top to then denaturalize somebody," he said. "We're talking about taking away a benefit and then banishing them from the United States."
FORMER USCIS OFFICIAL, ACCOMPLICE CHARGED IN ALLEGED $960K CITIZENSHIP BRIBERY SCHEME
Rep. Ilhan Omar, D-Minn., is denying that she has been made aware of any criminal investigation into her after White House border czar Tom Homan confirmed Sunday that the Department of Homeland Security is investigating her. (Daniel Heuer/Bloomberg via Getty Images; Eric Lee/Bloomberg via Getty Images)
For Omar to be denaturalized, the process would have to be related to allegations that she falsified information when obtaining her own citizenship in 2000. Omar claims she was granted automatic citizenship because she was a minor when her father was naturalized.
Congressional records state Omar became a citizen at age 17, but speculation that she was older at the time of her naturalization began after former Minnesota congressional candidate AJ Kern accused Omar’s birth year of being revised on the Minnesota Legislative Reference Library website.
This caused allegations to circulate on social media that she was not a minor at the time, which, if ever proven true, could lead to her denaturalization. Even if her father lied in his citizenship paperwork, this could also potentially lead to Omar being stripped of her citizenship.
Wildes also explained that the government makes a "case-by-case" decision when it comes to pursuing denaturalization cases. He also pointed out the relevancy of an intentional lie as opposed to a mistake.
"If the government were to prosecute for document fraud, we would also want to know whether or not she was represented by counsel, and if there were simple mistakes on her application or inadvertences that may be deemed to be fraudulent," Wildes said.
"Whether or not [these] things are truthful, hypothesized, or can be backed up in fact, will play heavily in that prosecution."
Homan didn't answer whether the federal government has evidence that Omar committed either marriage or immigration fraud , while also declining to go into detail about what particularly DHS is investigating Omar for.
Omar told Fox News Digital just last week that she has not been contacted by DHS or made aware of any ongoing investigation into her marriage or immigration status, saying she isn’t worried about it because "the right wing always had this s--- going."
'SQUAD' DEM DISMISSES FRAUD PROBE SPECULATION AFTER $29M NET-WORTH DROP
But Wildes said her being unaware that she is being investigated is not unusual and doesn’t invalidate Homan’s confirmation of a "criminal" investigation against her.
"The congresswoman's not being aware doesn't change anything," Wildes said. "There is no obligation for the government to show their hand, and they're going to want to make sure that they have a good prosecution, and they don't give anything up in the interim because of the politics that this presents as well."
"I haven't seen anything that I think is worthy of a prosecution," Wildes said. "This is a member of Congress. It may not be your politics, but we have to also make sure that we engage in prosecutions properly and not frivolously."

Neither Omar nor DHS responded to Fox News Digital’s requests for comment.

articles.title_orig: GOP senators push back on Trump’s taxpayer-funded ad
articles.title_zh: GOP senators push back on Trump’s taxpayer-funded ad
articles.content_orig:
Taxpayer money from U.S. Customs and Border Protection funded the pro-Trump television ads that have drawn bipartisan scrutiny just weeks before November's midterm election , The Wall Street Journal reported Tuesday.
President Donald Trump personally pushed for the ads and was involved in creating them, the Journal reported, citing people familiar with the matter.
The revelation puts a CBP, part of the Department of Homeland Security, behind a campaign that looks far different from its traditional public messaging. CBP routinely runs ads discouraging illegal immigration. These spots instead feature Trump heavily, tout his tax cuts , attack communism and recycle language from his 2024 campaign.
One ad declares that "America will never be a communist country" as images of Trump fill the screen. Another revives his "final battle" message from the 2024 race and attacks the political establishment and news media.
The ads have already aired thousands of times nationally and locally. CNBC previously reported that more than $1.2 million had been spent airing two of the spots, according to AdImpact, which tracks political advertising spending.
Democrats and at least one Republican senator have questioned whether taxpayer dollars should be used for ads centered so heavily on Trump. Some Democrats in Congress are now calling for investigations into whether money appropriated for border protection is being used to promote the president's political message.
"It appears DHS has dedicated $20 million to this outrageous scheme," Sens. Patty Murray , D-Wash., and Chris Murphy , D-Conn., wrote in a letter to DHS on Tuesday, saying the department tapped money provided to CBP through Republicans' " One Big Beautiful Bill Act ."
The pressure also spread to federal regulators Tuesday. Watchdog group Public Citizen filed a complaint with the Federal Communications Commission and Federal Trade Commission urging broadcasters to stop airing the ads, while separately asking the Government Accountability Office and Office of Special Counsel last Friday to investigate alleged violations of federal propaganda restrictions and the Hatch Act, which restricts the involvement of federal government employees in political campaigns.
The White House defended the campaign Tuesday, calling the spots public service announcements.
“These public service announcements are about reminding Americans to love their country and understand what makes it worth defending, at home, at our borders, and abroad,” a White House spokesperson told CNBC. “The ad is educational and unapologetically patriotic. We should be proud of our country.”
CBP did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

articles.title_zh: Bears call on QB3 Case Keenum in rousing victory over Eagles
articles.content_orig:
Monday night's game looked like an uphill battle earlier in the week.
The Eagles came into Chicago 2-0 and the Chicago Bears were without their dynamic quarterback and their young backup.
Starting a third-string quarterback, even at home, against a perennial playoff team is rarely a recipe for success.
But as fans are beginning to become accustomed to, Ben Johnson had other plans.
It was a familiar recipe at times, with the defense forcing three turnovers.
However, it was the passing game that carried the load early for Chicago.
Case Keenum looked like his Houston days in college, when he set all-time NCAA passing records that still stand.
Once the Bears took a 20-7 lead, the run game got going.
All in all, it was a very fun, team win for Chicago to move to 2-1 on the season and stay above .500 without Caleb Williams .
Case Keenum, QB – Who says 38-years-old is old?! Not your 38-year-old author. 247 yards passing, two touchdown passes and a game-sealing rushing TD. He was making plays at all levels of the field, not just dinking and dunking. It was as perfect as you would want from a third-string QB.
Kalif Raymond , WR – Three games into the season and weapons like Luther Burden III , Rome Odunze and Colston Loveland , who would have thought 32-year-old Raymond would be their leading receiver? Six catches, 90 yards and he capped it with a 41-yard touchdown that really blew the game open to Chicago's side.
Dillon Thieneman, S – The rookie led the Bears in tackles for the third straight game. He also notched his first career interception. He put himself in the absolute best spot, while former Bears QB Andy Dalton somehow didn't see him.
Rome Odunze, WR – Odunze continues to be confounding. He disappears for stretches in games, then he drops an open touchdown pass with no defenders around him and gets flagged for a false start on third-and-one near the goal line. But then he comes up with two or three big catches on a crucial drive. Here in year three, it's time to see more consistency from the former ninth-overall pick.
Jaylon Johnson , CB – Johnson has been up and down. He finished last night's game strong, with five tackles and a TFL. But he was getting beat and looked like he was playing from behind for much of the game. It's fair to wonder if he's ever going to be able to recapture his glory from a few years ago.
Sam Roush, TE – It's often hard to pick a third player for "down" after a big win like that, especially when both sides of the ball played so well. So maybe it's a choose-your-own-adventure here. But Roush diving on an already downed punt and causing a touchback was another rookie mistake just a week after a very rough outing against Minnesota . It's a tough learning curve, and hopefully the rookie and fans will look back on this as a small blip on a successful career.
Who is on your up and down lists this week? Let us know in the comments.

articles.title_zh: Framework’s Most Powerful Desktop Will Be Available For Pre-Order This Week, Featuring AMD’s Ryzen AI MAX+ 495 Chip, 192 GB Memory, As It Delivers A Strong AI Punch In A Tiny Box
articles.content_orig:
Framework has announced that its AMD Ryzen AI MAX+ 495 Desktop with 192 GB memory will be available for pre-order this Wednesday.
Yesterday, we covered a handful of announcements from AMD partners on their latest AMD Ryzen AI MAX+ 495 systems.
These top-of-the-line designs featuring impressive capabilities & 192GB of memory sure sound super enticing for AI users and professionals. There are going to be plenty of Ryzen AI MAX 400 systems to select from, with prices beyond the $5000 US mark, & Framework is also announcing the pre-order date for its upcoming Desktop PC.
We're opening pre-orders for the 192GB Framework Desktop this Wednesday morning Pacific Time.  This has AMD's new Ryzen AI Max+ Pro 495, an open-end x4 PCIe slot, a pre-installed Noctua fan, and an optional pre-built config with Fedora pre-loaded. pic.twitter.com/JfidMrtN9p
Framework Desktop is the same system that the company previewed at AMD's Advancing AI event a few months back . The system comes packed with the AMD Ryzen AI MAX+ 495 chip . This chip is an updated version of AMD's Ryzen AI MAX+ PRO 395, offering the same 16 Zen 5 cores but clocked at a higher 5.2 GHz frequency. The GPU is upgraded to the Radeon 8065S, which packs 40 RDNA 3.5 cores at 3.0 GHz.
For memory, the system packs an astonishing 192 GB of Unified memory , operating at 273 GB/s (8533 MT/s LPDDR5X), which is a 6.6% speed-up in memory speeds & bandwidth, and a 50% boost to capacity versus the Ryzen AI MAX+ 395 systems, which offered 256 GB/s bandwidth & up to 128 GB capacity.
According to Framework, the system is optimized for AI LLMs, running DeepSeek V4-Flash at Q8 on a single box, and there's room to spare for additional context length.
There are also several other improvements made to the new Framework AMD Ryzen AI MAX+ 495 Desktop, such as the PCIe x4 slot being open-ended, which would allow users to plug in larger PCIe cards directly within the system. To showcase its open-ended PCIe slots, Framework set up a concept of a cluster using two 50 GbE NICs, which enable RDMA over Ethernet (RoCE). This offers ultra-low latency and makes it possible to effectively pool 384 GB of memory across two desktops with tensor parallelism.
The company will also introduce a pre-built version with a Linux distro pre-loaded. Framework has stated that as LPDDR5X prices continue to rise, the 192 GB Ryzen AI MAX+ 495 system will bring a substantial jump in cost over the existing 128 GB model, and recommends picking up a 32GB, 64GB, or 128GB model based on your budget.
AMD's Ryzen AI MAX+ 495 with 192 GB will eclipse existing 128 GB platforms such as NVIDIA's DGX Spark, which still retains 128 GB LP5X memory and costs close to $5000 US. The base price of the MAX+ 395 system from Framework is around $3500 US , and that's also what most 395+ PCs are selling for from other manufacturers. We have seen various pre-order prices starting above $6000 US , so we expect a similar ballpark for the Framework Desktop when it hits pre-orders this Wednesday.
